coach_says: Your knight on b5 was attacked by the c4 pawn, and taking on c4 doesn't solve that: after bxc4 the new c4 pawn hits b5 again, your e4 pawn has lost its d5 support and hangs to Nxe4, and White's rook gets the open b-file. Your d5 and e4 pawns were your best asset, a connected central pair. Move the knight first (Nc7 also eyes the a6 pawn) and keep the pawn pair together; after cxd5 cxd5 you have two connected passed pawns.

Bd7 is a quiet move that does nothing about the centre, and it lets White play a3: after Bxc3 Bxc3 the bishop on c3 hits your queen on a5, so White gains time and keeps the two bishops. With White's king still in the middle, strike at the centre with ...e5: the d4 pawn is attacked twice (pawn and Nc6) and defended once, and if d5 then Nd4 hits the queen on b3. When you are ahead in development, open the centre rather than make waiting moves.
also: queen and bishop lined up on a5-b4

coach_says: b5 chases the queen but doesn't develop anything and loosens your queenside pawns, while your king is still in the centre and your c8 bishop is shut in. ...d5 also hits the queen and frees the bishop at the same time, and it is safe: White can't take en passant because the e5 pawn is pinned to the king by your queen on e7. When you have a choice of moves that attack something, pick the one that also develops.
also: pinned pawn can't take en passant

coach_says: g4 puts a pawn on a square nothing defends: your knight on h3 doesn't cover g4. Right now the c8 bishop is blocked by the d7 pawn, but one move ...d5 opens it and the g4 pawn simply falls. Before pushing a pawn, check who will defend it once the opponent opens the line onto it.

Taking on c4 looks like it wins a bishop, but your d5 pawn was the only thing standing between White's queen on d1 and your bishop on d7. Once the pawn leaves the d-file, Qxd7 takes your bishop back for free, and you're left with doubled c-pawns and White's queen deep in your camp. Before capturing with a pawn, ask what that pawn was blocking or guarding; Qb7 first, defending d7 along the rank, kept your central pawns and your bishop.

c6 is a reasonable way to challenge White's d5 pawn and is close to the best moves here. Just keep in mind your kingside is a little loose after ...f6, so plans like ...g6 and ...Bh6 to swap off your bad bishop, or ...Ne7 and ...g6, are worth knowing in this structure.
Castling is a perfectly sound move here and only slightly less precise than Bb3 or Nc3. Nothing in the position punishes it, so keep developing and look to make use of your space with c4 or a4 later.

Excellent: c3 blocks the check with gain of time, hitting the bishop on b4 while your Bb5 keeps the d7 knight pinned. This is the best move and wins material. Blocking a check with a move that also attacks something is exactly the habit to keep.
Good: taking the knight on b3 is the engine's top move, swapping pieces while you're a pawn up and keeping your strong knight on e5. Keep trading down toward an endgame where your extra pawn decides.

Bd6 is a sensible developing move, about as good as anything here. You're behind in material after the queen loss earlier, so the job now is to finish development, keep your king safe on g6 and look for chances; this move does that.
Recapturing with the knight is fine and practically as good as Kxe7. You win back the piece and keep a big advantage; next, watch your loose h-pawn and get your king safe.
Qd5 is one of several equal choices in a difficult position. You're a bit worse, so keeping your queen active and your c-pawns protected is the right approach.
e4 is close to the best move: it gains space and gives you a protected central pawn. Nf5 bringing the knight off the rim was slightly more accurate, so keep your pieces' activity in mind too.
Ne5 is a normal plan against this Stonewall-type setup and only a touch less accurate than c4. Fine; just make sure you follow up by challenging the centre with c4.

Your knight on f3 was the piece defending h4, and on h2 it also blocks your rook's protection along the h-file. Now Black's bishop on e7 can simply take the h4 pawn. Before moving a piece, check what it was guarding; here h5, kicking the queen, or d4, hitting the centre, were much better.

You gave up the exchange for an attack, so you need open lines, and Qf3+ works against that. The king just steps to e8, and your queen on f3 now blocks your own g2 bishop; after exd5 Black can take back with Qxd5 and offer a queen trade, which suits the side with more material. First take on d5: then Qxd5 is impossible because your bishop covers d5, and you keep Qf3+ for later.
also: avoid queen trades when material down

coach_says: You spotted Black's threat (Bxc4 and after dxc4 the rook on d8 takes your queen), but b3 defends it passively. Nxe5 meets it and wins a pawn: e5 is attacked by your knight and rook but defended only by the c6 knight, and Black's queen on e7 sits on the e-file behind the e6 bishop. If Black replies Bxc4, Nxc6 uncovers your rook onto the queen and hits d8 too. Look for pins on an open file before making a defensive move.
concept: win e5 using the e-file pin

coach_says: Your bishop on a2 was attacked by the queen on f2 along the second rank, and nothing defends it. Rbc8 goes after the c3 pawn but lets Qxa2+, winning the bishop with check. Before starting your own attack, check every piece of yours that's attacked; Be6 or Bf7 brings the bishop back to safety.

White's last move, Bb1, wasn't just a retreat: it opened the d-file, so the rook on d1 now attacks your knight on d4, which nothing defends. Rfc8 ignores that and Rxd4 wins a piece. When the opponent moves a piece away, ask what it uncovered; here Ne2+ saves the knight with check and then Rxa3 picks up a pawn.
concept: missed a discovered attack on your knight

coach_says: Your bishop had to move, but Bc4 lets Black play Bxb2: the g7 bishop takes your unprotected b2 pawn and then attacks the rook on a1, which can't easily get out. Use the check Qe6+ first: after Qe7, Bxd7+ wins back material and you keep the initiative. When a bishop sits on a long diagonal pointing at your corner, check that the pawn and rook on it are protected.
concept: loose b2 pawn and a1 rook
